Working Alone.name: Working Alone
Working Alone.description:
🃏 Last trains and old debts: a nameless broker is buying drinks for anyone with a fighting Quirk.

📍 The alley bars behind Musutafu's station arcade · night
🎭 You answer to no one
👥 For Independent Villains
Working Alone.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Sunday night, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy, an hour before the last train. The player character is a villain who works for no organization: a thief, a fence, an enforcer for hire, a crook with a cause, or someone one bad night from becoming one. The Background decides which; if it is silent, the PC came to collect money owed for a past job. Their business here is their own. The lanes hold a second piece of business tonight: a broker who never gives his name has been buying drinks for small-time crooks with fighting Quirks and handing out cash to anyone willing to take paid work against heroes. He says his client is the League of Villains, a name the lanes have barely heard. The police box at the north exit has heard the name once and filed it as bar talk.
THE PLACE: The Back Alleys of the Musutafu Station District: narrow lanes behind the Hero Merch Arcade, crowded with tiny bars, standing noodle counters, vending machines, delivery bikes and stacked crates. Office workers drink here until the last train; small-time crooks use the corners for deals and scores. The lanes smell of grilled skewers and garbage. Cars cannot fit, so patrol heroes cut through on foot. The local rule is to mind one's own business: nobody here wants to be a witness.
THE MOMENT: The PC waits at a standing noodle counter where a contact was supposed to meet them; the contact is late. Two stools down, a man in a cheap suit who calls himself Goto pays for everyone's beer in cash and asks the cook, loudly, who in the lane has a Quirk that can hurt a pro. At the far end of the lane, a patrol hero's voice carries over the bar noise.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Death Arms: walks the station blocks and charges in first, shouting warnings; any public Quirk use is his business.
- Kamui Woods: a capture specialist who binds several suspects at once; he cuts through the lanes on patrol, and fire is his weakness.
- Mount Lady: answers calls in the district, though these lanes are too narrow for her giant form, which she resents.
- Backdraft: shares a patrol garage with Death Arms and comes in for any fire or collapse.
- Sansa Tamakawa: the police officer who takes statements after a Quirk incident; he arrives with uniformed officers once someone calls it in.
The late contact is a generated person. The broker stays nameless and names no client beyond the League.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Criminal Ties: the late contact belongs to the PC's family's old circle, and the burner phone buzzes with a message that he will not be coming.
- Family Business: a bar owner in the lane recognizes the PC from the family shop and quietly asks for a favor that is not legal.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: the broker sizes the PC up on sight and offers twice the usual rate, because heroes already treat people like the PC as villains.
- Transformation: the cook mentions that a patrol hero asked about someone matching the PC's transformed shape after a robbery last week.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph features make them the one face in the lane nobody forgets, and a drunk office worker will not stop staring.
- Default: the contact arrives at last with a split lip, half the money, and someone following him into the lane.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Back Alleys; the arcade and the station are other areas.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; any public use is a crime and draws a patrol within minutes.
- The broker deals in talk and cash; he knows nothing of his client's plans, and the narrator does not supply them.
- Pros outclass a lone villain in a straight fight; escape, misdirection and the crowd are the PC's tools.
- End on the open moment, the broker's question still hanging in the lane, without writing the PC's choice.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- An independent villain's week is an ordinary life with a crime inside it. The PC sleeps where the Background says (a rented room, a family flat, a capsule hotel, a friend's sofa) and pays for it from work, legal or not.
- The Back Alleys run on the commuter clock: service lanes and delivery bikes by day, office workers drinking until the last train, empty lanes after it. The Convenience Store Corner at the north exit sells rice balls and coffee all night, and the police box there takes lost wallets and first reports.
- Money comes from the PC's own trade: a debt collected, goods fenced, a favor for a bar owner who pays in cash and silence.
- Each public use of the Quirk adds a line to a police description. A heteromorph body or a distinctive Quirk is hard to hide, so careful villains cover up and keep moving.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- The broker who calls himself Goto: generous while he is buying, remembers who turned him down, and moves to another lane when a patrol turns in.
- Death Arms and Backdraft: share a garage on Hero Agency Row; Death Arms grabs first and shouts warnings, Backdraft counts heads and puts out fires.
- Kamui Woods: binds several suspects at once and says little. Mount Lady needles him in public and hates these narrow lanes.
- Sansa Tamakawa: courteous, and writes down everything a witness says, descriptions included. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi takes over when a case grows; his Quirk tells him when he hears a lie.
- Giran: the best-known broker in Japan, who meets buyers in Yokohama's Chinatown; a lone villain reaches him only through an introduction and a fee.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Take Goto's beer and hear the pitch, or sell him a name from the lane.
- Follow him out when he leaves, to learn who pays him.
- Keep waiting for the contact, or go looking for them.
- Leave before the patrol reaches the counter.
- Tip off the police box about the broker, for money, a favor or a cleaner record.
MORE RULES:
- Goto's trail leads through other middlemen before it reaches anyone who speaks for the League.
- A lone villain's backup is whatever they arranged themselves: an arrest is theirs to escape or answer, and every favor owed gets collected.
Working Alone.firstQuest: Collect what is owed and stay free: decide what the broker's money is worth, and who in these lanes can be trusted to keep quiet.
Working Alone.questGenerationGuidance: Favor street-level crime with consequences: collecting debts, fencing stolen goods, a protection racket in the alley bars, small heists timed against patrol routes, rivals who want the same corner. The nameless broker's cash leads toward the League of Villains or toward selling him out; both stay open. Death Arms, Kamui Woods, Mount Lady and Backdraft work these streets and the police keep files, so heat builds with every public Quirk use. Offer jobs, never assign them. Keep an ordinary life under the crime: a rented room, a day job, a family that does not ask. The League's plans and any canon operation surface only through play, and the PC may join, profit from, sabotage or report them. Record debts, grudges and who holds a description of the PC. Let the PC's own goal set the arc: a debt to clear, a rival to beat, family to support, a grudge against a hero. Work in the lanes stays small and local until fences and bar owners know the PC's name. Heat fades only while the PC lies low, and the file stays open.
